description: SCOUT's Deep Umbra shadow model, ported from SCOUT (urban-toolkit/scout): a generator network that predicts how much of a season's day the ground spends in shadow, from zoom-16 building height tiles, the tile's latitude and the season. Its Accumulated Shadow node runs it on the height raster of SCOUT Rasters' Rasterize Buildings and returns the shadow in minutes, a raster that an Autark map draws and a Raster Calculator's statistics sum up. The weights are SCOUT's TensorFlow checkpoint ckpt-44, exported to ONNX by scripts/scout/export_deep_umbra.py; they ship in the Curio repository but not in the pip package.

name: Deep Umbra (accumulated shadows)

templates.description: SCOUT's accumulated shadow simulation: Deep Umbra, a generator network, predicts for each zoom-16 map tile how much of a season's day each cell spends in shadow, from the heights of the buildings on the tile and its eight neighbours, the tile's latitude and the season. Input: the raster of Rasterize Buildings: a RASTER of building heights in metres in EPSG:3395 on the zoom-16 tile grid. A tile with no data, which Rasterize Buildings gives a tile SCOUT wrote no file for, is not predicted. Output: one RASTER of the accumulated shadow in minutes on the input's grid, no data on the tiles not predicted, for an Autark map, band band_1. SCOUT's metrics, the mean and median accumulated shadow over the ground, are a Raster Calculator's statistics of this raster, with the heights on its input_1 as the mask and the ground where the height is under 1.08 m. The Widgets tab sets the season. The model is this package's, model.scout.deep-umbra.
